--- FILE: .venv\Lib\site-packages\lxml\isoschematron\resources\xsl\iso-schematron-xslt1\readme.txt ---
ISO SCHEMATRON 2010

XSLT implementation by Rick Jelliffe with assistance from members of Schematron-love-in maillist.

2010-04-21

Two distributions are available. One is for XSLT1 engines. 
The other is for XSLT2 engines, such as SAXON 9.


This version of Schematron splits the process into a pipeline of several different XSLT stages.

1) First, preprocess your Schematron schema with iso_dsdl_include.xsl.  
This is a macro processor to assemble the schema from various parts. 
If your schema is not in separate parts, you can skip this stage.
This stage also generates error messages for some common XPath syntax problems.

2) Second, preprocess the output from stage 1 with iso_abstract_expand.xsl.  
This is a macro processor to convert abstract patterns to real patterns. 
If your schema does not use abstract patterns, you can skip this
stage.

3) Third, compile the Schematron schema into an XSLT script. 
This will typically use iso_svrl_for_xslt1.xsl or iso_svrl_for_xslt2.xsl 
(which in turn invoke iso_schematron_skeleton_for_xslt1.xsl or iso_schematron_skeleton_for_saxon.xsl)
However, other "meta-stylesheets" are also in common use; the principle of operation is the same.
If your schema uses Schematron phases, supply these as command line/invocation parameters
to this process.

4) Fourth, run the script generated by stage 3 against the document being validated.
If you are using the SVRL script, then the output of validation will be an XML document.
If your schema uses Schematron parameters, supply these as command line/invocation parameters
to this process. 


The XSLT2 distribution also features several next generation features, 
such as validating multiple documents. See the source code for details.

Schematron assertions can be written in any language, of course; the file
sch-messages-en.xhtml contains the diagnostics messages from the XSLT2 skeleton
in English, and this can be used as template to localize the skeleton's
error messages. Note that typically programming errors in Schematron are XPath
errors, which requires localized messages from the XSLT engine.

ANT
---
To give an example of how to process a document, here is a sample ANT task.

<target  name="schematron-compile-test" >

	   <!-- expand inclusions -->
	   <xslt basedir="test/schematron"
	   		style="iso_dsdl_include.xsl" in="test.sch"  out="test1.sch"> 
	   				<classpath>
	   					<pathelement location="${lib.dir}/saxon9.jar"/>
	   				</classpath>
	   </xslt>

	   <!-- expand abstract patterns -->
	   <xslt basedir="test/schematron"
	   		style="iso_abstract_expand.xsl" in="test1.sch"  out="test2.sch"> 
	   				<classpath>
	   					<pathelement location="${lib.dir}/saxon9.jar"/>
	   				</classpath>
	   </xslt>



	   <!-- compile it -->
	   <xslt basedir="test/schematron"
	   		style="iso_svrl_for_xslt2.xsl" in="test2.sch"  out="test.xsl"> 
	   				<classpath>
	   					<pathelement location="${lib.dir}/saxon9.jar"/>
	   				</classpath>
	   </xslt>
	   
	   <!-- validate -->
	   <xslt basedir="test/schematron"
		   		style="test.xsl" in="instance.xml"  out="instance.svrlt"> 
		   				<classpath>
		   					<pathelement location="${lib.dir}/saxon9.jar"/>
		   				</classpath>
	</xslt>
		</target>

--- FILE: .venv\Lib\site-packages\numpy\ma\README.rst ---
==================================
A guide to masked arrays in NumPy
==================================

.. Contents::

See http://www.scipy.org/scipy/numpy/wiki/MaskedArray (dead link)
for updates of this document.


History
-------

As a regular user of MaskedArray, I (Pierre G.F. Gerard-Marchant) became
increasingly frustrated with the subclassing of masked arrays (even if
I can only blame my inexperience). I needed to develop a class of arrays
that could store some additional information along with numerical values,
while keeping the possibility for missing data (picture storing a series
of dates along with measurements, what would later become the `TimeSeries
Scikit <http://projects.scipy.org/scipy/scikits/wiki/TimeSeries>`__
(dead link).

I started to implement such a class, but then quickly realized that
any additional information disappeared when processing these subarrays
(for example, adding a constant value to a subarray would erase its
dates). I ended up writing the equivalent of *numpy.core.ma* for my
particular class, ufuncs included. Everything went fine until I needed to
subclass my new class, when more problems showed up: some attributes of
the new subclass were lost during processing. I identified the culprit as
MaskedArray, which returns masked ndarrays when I expected masked
arrays of my class. I was preparing myself to rewrite *numpy.core.ma*
when I forced myself to learn how to subclass ndarrays. As I became more
familiar with the *__new__* and *__array_finalize__* methods,
I started to wonder why masked arrays were objects, and not ndarrays,
and whether it wouldn't be more convenient for subclassing if they did
behave like regular ndarrays.

The new *maskedarray* is what I eventually come up with. The
main differences with the initial *numpy.core.ma* package are
that MaskedArray is now a subclass of *ndarray* and that the
*_data* section can now be any subclass of *ndarray*. Apart from a
couple of issues listed below, the behavior of the new MaskedArray
class reproduces the old one. Initially the *maskedarray*
implementation was marginally slower than *numpy.ma* in some areas,
but work is underway to speed it up; the expectation is that it can be
made substantially faster than the present *numpy.ma*.


Note that if the subclass has some special methods and
attributes, they are not propagated to the masked version:
this would require a modification of the *__getattribute__*
method (first trying *ndarray.__getattribute__*, then trying
*self._data.__getattribute__* if an exception is raised in the first
place), which really slows things down.

Main differences
----------------

 * The *_data* part of the masked array can be any subclass of ndarray (but not recarray, cf below).
 * *fill_value* is now a property, not a function.
 * in the majority of cases, the mask is forced to *nomask* when no value is actually masked. A notable exception is when a masked array (with no masked values) has just been unpickled.
 * I got rid of the *share_mask* flag, I never understood its purpose.
 * *put*, *putmask* and *take* now mimic the ndarray methods, to avoid unpleasant surprises. Moreover, *put* and *putmask* both update the mask when needed.  * if *a* is a masked array, *bool(a)* raises a *ValueError*, as it does with ndarrays.
 * in the same way, the comparison of two masked arrays is a masked array, not a boolean
 * *filled(a)* returns an array of the same subclass as *a._data*, and no test is performed on whether it is contiguous or not.
 * the mask is always printed, even if it's *nomask*, which makes things easy (for me at least) to remember that a masked array is used.
 * *cumsum* works as if the *_data* array was filled with 0. The mask is preserved, but not updated.
 * *cumprod* works as if the *_data* array was filled with 1. The mask is preserved, but not updated.

New features
------------

This list is non-exhaustive...

 * the *mr_* function mimics *r_* for masked arrays.
 * the *anom* method returns the anomalies (deviations from the average)

Using the new package with numpy.core.ma
----------------------------------------

I tried to make sure that the new package can understand old masked
arrays. Unfortunately, there's no upward compatibility.

For example:

>>> import numpy.core.ma as old_ma
>>> import maskedarray as new_ma
>>> x = old_ma.array([1,2,3,4,5], mask=[0,0,1,0,0])
>>> x
array(data =
 [     1      2 999999      4      5],
      mask =
 [False False True False False],
      fill_value=999999)
>>> y = new_ma.array([1,2,3,4,5], mask=[0,0,1,0,0])
>>> y
array(data = [1 2 -- 4 5],
      mask = [False False True False False],
      fill_value=999999)
>>> x==y
array(data =
 [True True True True True],
      mask =
 [False False True False False],
      fill_value=?)
>>> old_ma.getmask(x) == new_ma.getmask(x)
array([True, True, True, True, True])
>>> old_ma.getmask(y) == new_ma.getmask(y)
array([True, True, False, True, True])
>>> old_ma.getmask(y)
False


Using maskedarray with matplotlib
---------------------------------

Starting with matplotlib 0.91.2, the masked array importing will work with
the maskedarray branch) as well as with earlier versions.

By default matplotlib still uses numpy.ma, but there is an rcParams setting
that you can use to select maskedarray instead.  In the matplotlibrc file
you will find::

  #maskedarray : False       # True to use external maskedarray module
                             # instead of numpy.ma; this is a temporary #
                             setting for testing maskedarray.


Uncomment and set to True to select maskedarray everywhere.
Alternatively, you can test a script with maskedarray by using a
command-line option, e.g.::

  python simple_plot.py --maskedarray


Masked records
--------------

Like *numpy.ma.core*, the *ndarray*-based implementation
of MaskedArray is limited when working with records: you can
mask any record of the array, but not a field in a record. If you
need this feature, you may want to give the *mrecords* package
a try (available in the *maskedarray* directory in the scipy
sandbox). This module defines a new class, *MaskedRecord*. An
instance of this class accepts a *recarray* as data, and uses two
masks: the *fieldmask* has as many entries as records in the array,
each entry with the same fields as a record, but of boolean types:
they indicate whether the field is masked or not; a record entry
is flagged as masked in the *mask* array if all the fields are
masked. A few examples in the file should give you an idea of what
can be done. Note that *mrecords* is still experimental...

Optimizing maskedarray
----------------------

Should masked arrays be filled before processing or not?
--------------------------------------------------------

In the current implementation, most operations on masked arrays involve
the following steps:

 * the input arrays are filled
 * the operation is performed on the filled arrays
 * the mask is set for the results, from the combination of the input masks and the mask corresponding to the domain of the operation.

For example, consider the division of two masked arrays::

  import numpy
  import maskedarray as ma
  x = ma.array([1,2,3,4],mask=[1,0,0,0], dtype=numpy.float64)
  y = ma.array([-1,0,1,2], mask=[0,0,0,1], dtype=numpy.float64)

The division of x by y is then computed as::

  d1 = x.filled(0) # d1 = array([0., 2., 3., 4.])
  d2 = y.filled(1) # array([-1.,  0.,  1.,  1.])
  m = ma.mask_or(ma.getmask(x), ma.getmask(y)) # m =
  array([True,False,False,True])
  dm = ma.divide.domain(d1,d2) # array([False,  True, False, False])
  result = (d1/d2).view(MaskedArray) # masked_array([-0. inf, 3., 4.])
  result._mask = logical_or(m, dm)

Note that a division by zero takes place. To avoid it, we can consider
to fill the input arrays, taking the domain mask into account, so that::

  d1 = x._data.copy() # d1 = array([1., 2., 3., 4.])
  d2 = y._data.copy() # array([-1.,  0.,  1.,  2.])
  dm = ma.divide.domain(d1,d2) # array([False,  True, False, False])
  numpy.putmask(d2, dm, 1) # d2 = array([-1.,  1.,  1.,  2.])
  m = ma.mask_or(ma.getmask(x), ma.getmask(y)) # m =
  array([True,False,False,True])
  result = (d1/d2).view(MaskedArray) # masked_array([-1. 0., 3., 2.])
  result._mask = logical_or(m, dm)

Note that the *.copy()* is required to avoid updating the inputs with
*putmask*.  The *.filled()* method also involves a *.copy()*.

A third possibility consists in avoid filling the arrays::

  d1 = x._data # d1 = array([1., 2., 3., 4.])
  d2 = y._data # array([-1.,  0.,  1.,  2.])
  dm = ma.divide.domain(d1,d2) # array([False,  True, False, False])
  m = ma.mask_or(ma.getmask(x), ma.getmask(y)) # m =
  array([True,False,False,True])
  result = (d1/d2).view(MaskedArray) # masked_array([-1. inf, 3., 2.])
  result._mask = logical_or(m, dm)

Note that here again the division by zero takes place.

A quick benchmark gives the following results:

 * *numpy.ma.divide*  : 2.69 ms per loop
 * classical division     : 2.21 ms per loop
 * division w/ prefilling : 2.34 ms per loop
 * division w/o filling   : 1.55 ms per loop

So, is it worth filling the arrays beforehand ? Yes, if we are interested
in avoiding floating-point exceptions that may fill the result with infs
and nans. No, if we are only interested into speed...


Thanks
------

I'd like to thank Paul Dubois, Travis Oliphant and Sasha for the
original masked array package: without you, I would never have started
that (it might be argued that I shouldn't have anyway, but that's
another story...).  I also wish to extend these thanks to Reggie Dugard
and Eric Firing for their suggestions and numerous improvements.


Revision notes
--------------

  * 08/25/2007 : Creation of this page
  * 01/23/2007 : The package has been moved to the SciPy sandbox, and is regularly updated: please check out your SVN version!

--- FILE: .venv\Lib\site-packages\pip\_vendor\README.rst ---
================
Vendoring Policy
================

* Vendored libraries **MUST** not be modified except as required to
  successfully vendor them.
* Vendored libraries **MUST** be released copies of libraries available on
  PyPI.
* Vendored libraries **MUST** be available under a license that allows
  them to be integrated into ``pip``, which is released under the MIT license.
* Vendored libraries **MUST** be accompanied with LICENSE files.
* The versions of libraries vendored in pip **MUST** be reflected in
  ``pip/_vendor/vendor.txt``.
* Vendored libraries **MUST** function without any build steps such as ``2to3``
  or compilation of C code, practically this limits to single source 2.x/3.x and
  pure Python.
* Any modifications made to libraries **MUST** be noted in
  ``pip/_vendor/README.rst`` and their corresponding patches **MUST** be
  included ``tools/vendoring/patches``.
* Vendored libraries should have corresponding ``vendored()`` entries in
  ``pip/_vendor/__init__.py``.

Rationale
=========

Historically pip has not had any dependencies except for ``setuptools`` itself,
choosing instead to implement any functionality it needed to prevent needing
a dependency. However, starting with pip 1.5, we began to replace code that was
implemented inside of pip with reusable libraries from PyPI. This brought the
typical benefits of reusing libraries instead of reinventing the wheel like
higher quality and more battle tested code, centralization of bug fixes
(particularly security sensitive ones), and better/more features for less work.

However, there are several issues with having dependencies in the traditional
way (via ``install_requires``) for pip. These issues are:

**Fragility**
   When pip depends on another library to function then if for whatever reason
   that library either isn't installed or an incompatible version is installed
   then pip ceases to function. This is of course true for all Python
   applications, however for every application *except* for pip the way you fix
   it is by re-running pip. Obviously, when pip can't run, you can't use pip to
   fix pip, so you're left having to manually resolve dependencies and
   installing them by hand.

**Making other libraries uninstallable**
   One of pip's current dependencies is the ``requests`` library, for which pip
   requires a fairly recent version to run.  If pip depended on ``requests`` in
   the traditional manner, then we'd either have to maintain compatibility with
   every ``requests`` version that has ever existed (and ever will), OR allow
   pip to render certain versions of ``requests`` uninstallable. (The second
   issue, although technically true for any Python application, is magnified by
   pip's ubiquity; pip is installed by default in Python, in ``pyvenv``, and in
   ``virtualenv``.)

**Security**
   This might seem puzzling at first glance, since vendoring has a tendency to
   complicate updating dependencies for security updates, and that holds true
   for pip. However, given the *other* reasons for avoiding dependencies, the
   alternative is for pip to reinvent the wheel itself.  This is what pip did
   historically. It forced pip to re-implement its own HTTPS verification
   routines as a workaround for the Python standard library's lack of SSL
   validation, which resulted in similar bugs in the validation routine in
   ``requests`` and ``urllib3``, except that they had to be discovered and
   fixed independently. Even though we're vendoring, reusing libraries keeps
   pip more secure by relying on the great work of our dependencies, *and*
   allowing for faster, easier security fixes by simply pulling in newer
   versions of dependencies.

**Bootstrapping**
   Currently most popular methods of installing pip rely on pip's
   self-contained nature to install pip itself. These tools work by bundling a
   copy of pip, adding it to ``sys.path``, and then executing that copy of pip.
   This is done instead of implementing a "mini installer" (to reduce
   duplication); pip already knows how to install a Python package, and is far
   more battle-tested than any "mini installer" could ever possibly be.

Many downstream redistributors have policies against this kind of bundling, and
instead opt to patch the software they distribute to debundle it and make it
rely on the global versions of the software that they already have packaged
(which may have its own patches applied to it). We (the pip team) would prefer
it if pip was *not* debundled in this manner due to the above reasons and
instead we would prefer it if pip would be left intact as it is now.

In the longer term, if someone has a *portable* solution to the above problems,
other than the bundling method we currently use, that doesn't add additional
problems that are unreasonable then we would be happy to consider, and possibly
switch to said method. This solution must function correctly across all of the
situation that we expect pip to be used and not mandate some external mechanism
such as OS packages.


Modifications
=============

* ``setuptools`` is completely stripped to only keep ``pkg_resources``.
* ``pkg_resources`` has been modified to import its dependencies from
  ``pip._vendor``, and to use the vendored copy of ``platformdirs``
  rather than ``appdirs``.
* ``packaging`` has been modified to import its dependencies from
  ``pip._vendor``.
* ``CacheControl`` has been modified to import its dependencies from
  ``pip._vendor``.
* ``requests`` has been modified to import its other dependencies from
  ``pip._vendor`` and to *not* load ``simplejson`` (all platforms) and
  ``pyopenssl`` (Windows).
* ``platformdirs`` has been modified to import its submodules from ``pip._vendor.platformdirs``.

Automatic Vendoring
===================

Vendoring is automated via the `vendoring <https://pypi.org/project/vendoring/>`_ tool from the content of
``pip/_vendor/vendor.txt`` and the different patches in
``tools/vendoring/patches``.
Launch it via ``vendoring sync . -v`` (requires ``vendoring>=0.2.2``).
Tool configuration is done via ``pyproject.toml``.

To update the vendored library versions, we have a session defined in ``nox``.
The command to upgrade everything is::

    nox -s vendoring -- --upgrade-all --skip setuptools

We do not upgrade ``setuptools``, because we only rely on ``pkg_resources``,
and tracking every ``setuptools`` change is unnecessary for our needs.


Managing Local Patches
======================

The ``vendoring`` tool automatically applies our local patches, but updating,
the patches sometimes no longer apply cleanly. In that case, the update will
fail. To resolve this, take the following steps:

1. Revert any incomplete changes in the revendoring branch, to ensure you have
   a clean starting point.
2. Run the revendoring of the library with a problem again: ``nox -s vendoring
   -- --upgrade <library_name>``.
3. This will fail again, but you will have the original source in your working
   directory. Review the existing patch against the source, and modify the patch
   to reflect the new version of the source. If you ``git add`` the changes the
   vendoring made, you can modify the source to reflect the patch file and then
   generate a new patch with ``git diff``.
4. Now, revert everything *except* the patch file changes. Leave the modified
   patch file unstaged but saved in the working tree.
5. Re-run the vendoring. This time, it should pick up the changed patch file
   and apply it cleanly. The patch file changes will be committed along with the
   revendoring, so the new commit should be ready to test and publish as a PR.


Debundling
==========

As mentioned in the rationale, we, the pip team, would prefer it if pip was not
debundled (other than optionally ``pip/_vendor/requests/cacert.pem``) and that
pip was left intact. However, if you insist on doing so, we have a
semi-supported method (that we don't test in our CI) and requires a bit of
extra work on your end in order to solve the problems described above.

1. Delete everything in ``pip/_vendor/`` **except** for
   ``pip/_vendor/__init__.py`` and ``pip/_vendor/vendor.txt``.
2. Generate wheels for each of pip's dependencies (and any of their
   dependencies) using your patched copies of these libraries. These must be
   placed somewhere on the filesystem that pip can access (``pip/_vendor`` is
   the default assumption).
3. Modify ``pip/_vendor/__init__.py`` so that the ``DEBUNDLED`` variable is
   ``True``.
4. Upon installation, the ``INSTALLER`` file in pip's own ``dist-info``
   directory should be set to something other than ``pip``, so that pip
   can detect that it wasn't installed using itself.
5. *(optional)* If you've placed the wheels in a location other than
   ``pip/_vendor/``, then modify ``pip/_vendor/__init__.py`` so that the
   ``WHEEL_DIR`` variable points to the location you've placed them.
6. *(optional)* Update the ``pip_self_version_check`` logic to use the
   appropriate logic for determining the latest available version of pip and
   prompt the user with the correct upgrade message.

Note that partial debundling is **NOT** supported. You need to prepare wheels
for all dependencies for successful debundling.

### Maven Parent overrides

Due to Maven's design, elements are inherited from the parent POM to the project POM.
While most of the inheritance is fine, it also inherits unwanted elements like `<license>` and `<developers>` from the parent.
To prevent this, the project POM contains empty overrides for these elements.
If you manually switch to a different parent and actually want the inheritance, you need to remove those overrides.


--- FILE: backend\pom.xml ---

		<version>4.1.0</version>
		<relativePath/> <!-- lookup parent from repository -->
	</parent>

	<name>backend</name>

	<url/>

	</licenses>

	</scm>

	</properties>

			<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
			<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>

		</dependency>

		</dependency>

# Fantacalcio Intelligence - Backend Production Runbook

## Purpose

This runbook describes the minimum safe production configuration for the
Fantacalcio Intelligence Spring Boot backend.

The production profile is `prod`.

## Required environment variables

The production profile intentionally has no fallback for credentials or
database connection values.

Required:

- `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod`
- `DATABASE_URL`
- `DATABASE_USERNAME`
- `DATABASE_PASSWORD`
- `ADMIN_USERNAME`
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
- `APP_USER_USERNAME`
- `APP_USER_PASSWORD`
- `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`

Optional:

- `SERVER_PORT` - default `8080`
- `DATA_REFRESH_SCHEDULER_ENABLED` - default `false`
- `DATA_REFRESH_SCHEDULER_CRON` - default `0 0 4 * * *`
- `DATA_REFRESH_SCHEDULER_SEASON` - default `2026/2027`

`CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is a comma-separated allow-list. Never use `*`.

Example:

`https://app.example.com,https://admin.example.com`

## Secret rules

Never commit production passwords.

Use long random values for `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `APP_USER_PASSWORD` and
`DATABASE_PASSWORD`.

Development defaults from `application.properties` must never be reused in
production.

## Database

Production uses Flyway as the schema authority.

Hibernate remains:

`spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`

Startup must fail if the database schema does not match the application.

Before deploying a new migration:

1. back up PostgreSQL;
2. verify the migration on the test database;
3. deploy the application;
4. verify Flyway startup logs;
5. verify `/actuator/health/readiness`.

## Health checks

Public health endpoints:

- `/actuator/health`
- `/actuator/health/liveness`
- `/actuator/health/readiness`

Detailed health information is hidden in production.

Recommended platform checks:

- liveness: `/actuator/health/liveness`
- readiness: `/actuator/health/readiness`

Do not use application business endpoints as infrastructure health probes.

## Security

The backend is stateless.

Admin endpoints under `/api/v1/admin/**` require the `ADMIN` role.

Basic Auth passwords are encoded before they are stored in the in-memory
Spring Security user store.

CORS uses an explicit allow-list supplied by `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

## Data refresh scheduler

The scheduler is disabled by default, including in production.

Enable it only after:

1. source import operations are stable;
2. source freshness is being monitored;
3. the expected season is configured;
4. scheduled refresh failures are monitored.

The freshness gate prevents a refresh from silently using stale required
sources.

## Deployment verification

After each deployment verify:

1. application startup is successful;
2. Flyway reports the expected schema version;
3. `/actuator/health` returns `UP`;
4. `/actuator/health/liveness` returns `UP`;
5. `/actuator/health/readiness` returns `UP`;
6. an admin endpoint rejects unauthenticated requests;
7. an admin endpoint accepts valid admin credentials;
8. `/api/v1/admin/data-freshness` returns the expected source state;
9. `/api/v1/admin/catalog/readiness` has no unexpected blocker;
10. Git working tree and release commit are clean.

## Shutdown

Spring Boot graceful shutdown is enabled.

The process should receive a normal termination signal and be allowed to
finish active requests before the platform force-kills it.

--- FILE: documentation\fantasy-player-value-model-v1.md ---
# Fantasy Player Value Model V1

## Scope and boundaries

`B50_FANTASY_VALUE_V1` is a deterministic, rule-based historical fantasy-football value model for the 495 current operational 2026/2027 players. Its only input is the immutable `B49_FEATURES_V1` evidence layer for 2024/2025 and 2025/2026. It does not use age, market value, reputation, league factors, current form, prices, calendar or newly acquired data.

Fantacalcio is authoritative for fantasy average, rating, PV and goalkeeper evidence. Transfermarkt contributes only certified usage, production and discipline. Missing fantasy evidence for international players remains `NULL`, never zero and never an invented proxy.

## Components and role models

All available components are on 0â€“100 role-relative scales. Fantasy quality uses 80% Fantacalcio fantasy-average role percentile and 20% a B50-derived role percentile of average rating when both exist. Usage reuses the source-aware B49 usage percentile. Production uses the mean of available B49 goal/assist rate percentiles; Fantacalcio rows use source-and-role-relative latest raw goal/assist percentiles because minutes do not exist. The signals are combined once, avoiding raw/per-90 double counting within a player.

Consistency is inverse role percentile of absolute comparable-season change and exists only for two same-source seasons. Discipline is the inverse role percentile of certified Transfermarkt discipline events per 90 after B49 small-sample exclusion. Goalkeeper-specific value combines penalties-saved percentile (60%) and inverse goals-conceded-per-PV percentile (40%); raw goals conceded are never used. Offensive production is excluded for goalkeepers.

Base weights are:

- P: fantasy quality 45, usage 30, goalkeeper 20, consistency 5.
- D: fantasy quality 40, usage 30, production 15, consistency 10, discipline 5.
- C: fantasy quality 35, production 30, usage 20, consistency 10, discipline 5.
- A: production 40, fantasy quality 35, usage 15, consistency 7, discipline 3.

These deliberately simple weights follow the audited availability and the fantasy-first role priorities. Trend/consistency remains at most 10%.

## Null, confidence and ranking contract

`NULL` stays `NULL`. Available base weights are renormalized to sum to 1.0; at least two meaningful components are required. Otherwise the final score/rank/percentile is `NULL` and status is `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`. B49 confidence is copied unchanged and remains separate; it never multiplies value.

Ranks are per role only. Competition ranking is used for equal unrounded scores, with player ID providing deterministic display order but no semantic tie break. Role percentile is inclusive 0â€“100 with average ranks for ties. Component/final/percentile display precision is two decimals; contributions use four decimals, while calculations occur before rounding.

## Versioning, persistence and limitations

The database grain is player, reference season and algorithm version. Import is append-only and idempotent; changed output under the same key is a conflict. Formula changes require a new version. Source-mix distributions, component coverage/distributions, correlations, anomalies, golden cases and top/bottom ranks are published under `data/statistics/value-model`.

The principal limitation is structural source coverage: international-only players have no manufactured fantasy quality, Fantacalcio-only players have no minute-based discipline, and profiles with fewer than two valid components are explicitly unranked. This is evidence uncertainty, not low player value.

--- FILE: documentation\identity-enrichment.md ---
# Identity enrichment (Block 46)

Identity enrichment is deliberately separate from player reconciliation and statistical links.
It never writes `player_source_mappings`, never changes `player_reconciliation_results.sources_count`,
and never lets FBref determine identity or fantasy role.

The reproducible input is the local 2026/27 catalog plus verified local aliases. Wikidata is queried
through its documented structured API by exact Wikipedia title in small batches with an identifying
User-Agent. No web-page scraping, fuzzy search crawling, CAPTCHA bypass, or rate-limit retry is used.
Wikidata entity IDs, URLs, confidence, observation/import timestamps, and minimal JSON evidence are
stored per field. The API returned HTTP 429 for the secondary country-code lookup; the pipeline
therefore preserved nationality as NULL and did not retry aggressively.

The second pass also uses the locally acquired 2026/27 Transfermarkt master (638 unique players,
20 teams) without any network access. A verified `FANTAMARKT` mapping in the form
`TRANSFERMARKT-<numeric-id>` is a deterministic stable anchor. Otherwise HIGH requires an exact
verified multi-token full name, coherent current club, and a unique master candidate, or an exact
verified alias plus independently known DOB, coherent club, and uniqueness. Surname plus club is
always REVIEW. The project name `FANTAMARKT` is intentionally retained in reconciliation; the new
`TRANSFERMARKT` provenance source belongs only to the identity profile.

`VERIFIED_COMPLETE` and `VERIFIED_PARTIAL` require HIGH confidence, a canonical full name, an exact
birth date, a stable Wikidata QID, and independent corroboration by the locally available FBref full
name and birth year. Exact title without that corroboration is `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; absent source data
is `DATA_SOURCE_MISSING`; an explicit local coverage classification may produce
`NO_SERIE_A_HISTORY_EXPECTED`. Partial dates such as `YYYY-00-00` are rejected.

The FBref matcher accepts HIGH only for an exact, unique enriched full name plus exact birth year.
The same FBref ID can propagate that anchor across seasons if no conflict exists. Current/historical
club, role, nationality, surname, fuzzy similarity, or an exact name alone are never sufficient.
Two FBref IDs converging on one player, or one FBref ID producing conflicting players, are REVIEW.

The separate identity readiness endpoint is `GET /api/v1/admin/identity/readiness?season=2026/2027`. Missing historical
coverage for a legitimate new arrival does not block the Catalog Quality Gate. CSV import is
idempotent and available at `POST /api/v1/admin/imports/identity/csv`; it updates only NULL player
fields from HIGH verified rows and rejects conflicting existing values atomically.
Migration V43 adds nationality text and the unique numeric Transfermarkt identity key and extends
allowed provenance fields/sources; V42 remains unchanged because it has already been exercised by Flyway.

--- FILE: documentation\player-performance-feature-model-v1.md ---
# Player Performance Feature Model V1

## Scope and decision

`B49_FEATURES_V1` is an immutable, deterministic evidence layer for the 495 players with an `ACTIVE` 2026/2027 registration. It derives features only from the certified Block 48 Fantacalcio and Transfermarkt history for 2024/2025 and 2025/2026. It does not acquire data, change identity, roles, registrations, clubs or raw statistics.

The model deliberately publishes component features and a data-confidence score, not a performance ranking. `historical_performance_score` and `cross_league_adjustment` are always `NULL`; the recorded decision is `OVERALL_SCORE_DEFERRED_TO_BLOCK_50`. No source-quality or league-strength coefficients were invented.

## Season source selection

The logical grain is player Ã— historical season. A meaningful Fantacalcio row is preferred because it is the certified Serie A source. Otherwise, Transfermarkt rows classified as `DOMESTIC_LEAGUE` are aggregated across clubs. Domestic cups, international cups, promotion/relegation/play-off competitions and all other rows remain supplemental evidence and never inflate the main season features.

Fantacalcio `appearances` means PV (partite a voto), not physical appearances. It is therefore stored as `fantacalcio_voted_appearances`; Transfermarkt appearances remain separate. Fantacalcio has no minutes, so minutes and per-90 features are never estimated for it.

## Null and aggregation policy

Unknown never becomes zero. Transfermarkt multi-club totals use strict-null aggregation: if any included domestic-league row has an unknown metric, the aggregate metric is `NULL`. Explicit zero remains zero. A per-90 value is emitted only when both its numerator and positive minutes are known:

`rate_per_90 = metric Ã— 90 / minutes_played`

Trends are calculated only between comparable source semantics. Transfermarkt-to-Transfermarkt supports minutes and per-90 deltas. Fantacalcio-to-Fantacalcio supports fantasy-average trend. Mixed-source pairs deliberately have no trend.

## Roles and percentiles

Percentiles are calculated independently inside the current P/D/C/A role. They use inclusive 0â€“100 rank and average ranks for ties. Missing values stay `NULL`. Goalkeepers have no goal-rate or assist-rate percentile; their certified Fantacalcio rating, fantasy average, goals conceded and penalties saved remain available.

Usage is source-specific: Fantacalcio PV and Transfermarkt minutes are ranked separately and are never combined into one numeric population. Rate percentiles require an eligible Transfermarkt sample.

## Small-sample policy

The V1 threshold is empirical, not arbitrary: the overall 25th percentile of positive, aggregated Transfermarkt domestic-league minutes in the certified current-player history. The generated audit records 297 samples and a threshold of 1,057 minutes. Raw per-90 values remain visible below the threshold, but rate percentiles are `NULL` and `small_sample_flag` is true.

## Confidence score

`data_confidence_score` measures evidence completeness, never player quality. It is the unweighted mean of four transparent components:

- season coverage: 50 points per available historical season;
- latest usage evidence: 100 when Fantacalcio PV or Transfermarkt minutes are known, otherwise 0;
- latest production completeness: 100 when goals and assists are known, 50 when only one is known, otherwise 0;
- fantasy evidence: 100 when at least one Fantacalcio season exists, otherwise 0.

The score is constrained to 0â€“100 and its components are persisted in `evidence`. Performance features are not multiplied by confidence.

## Versioning and persistence

The database key is `(player_id, reference_season_id, algorithm_version)`. The certified importer is append-only: an identical rerun inserts nothing; the same version with changed definitions, fingerprint, context or JSON is rejected. A future algorithm must use a new version and may coexist with V1. Foreign keys, uniqueness, role/history/source bounds, confidence bounds, JSON object checks, SHA-256 shape and the deferred-score policy are enforced by migration V48.

The input fingerprint is SHA-256 over the algorithm version and canonical selected season rows. Generated timestamps are database metadata and are excluded from the deterministic artifacts.

## Reproduction

1. Export the certified current context with `scripts/statistics/export_player_performance_context.ps1`.
2. Run `python scripts/statistics/build_player_performance_features.py`.
3. Run `python -m unittest scripts/statistics/test_player_performance_features.py`.
4. Apply V48, then run the certified importer first with `-Preflight`, then twice without it.

Primary auditable artifacts live in `data/statistics/features/`: the season base, compact import, wide feature review, definition catalog, source availability matrix, minutes distribution, anomalies and golden-player audit.

--- FILE: documentation\production-deployment-runbook.md ---
# Fantacalcio Intelligence â€” Production Deployment Runbook

This runbook is the provider-neutral input for D02. It assumes the certified strategy: one Linux VM/VPS for the Spring Boot JAR and reverse proxy, a PostgreSQL 17 instance (managed where available), and static frontend assets served by the reverse proxy. No production secrets belong in Git.

## 1. Infrastructure prerequisites

- A Linux VM/VPS with Java 21, a dedicated non-root service user, firewall access only for SSH, HTTP and HTTPS, and enough disk for two backend releases plus logs.
- PostgreSQL 17, preferably managed, with encrypted connections, automated backups and point-in-time recovery when available.
- A DNS name for the application and a TLS certificate issued by a trusted CA.
- Nginx, Caddy or an equivalent reverse proxy capable of static hosting, SPA fallback, TLS termination and proxying `/api/v1/` and `/actuator/`.
- Build workstation/CI with Node 22, npm 10+ and the repository Maven Wrapper. Build artifacts must be traceable to a release commit.
- Store secrets in the provider secret manager or a root/service-readable environment file outside the release directory.

Create release directories such as:

```text
/opt/fantacalcio/releases/<release-id>/backend.jar
/opt/fantacalcio/releases/<release-id>/frontend/
/opt/fantacalcio/current -> /opt/fantacalcio/releases/<release-id>
/etc/fantacalcio/backend.env
```

## 2. PostgreSQL creation

Create a dedicated database and least-privilege application role. Do not use the PostgreSQL superuser at runtime.

```sql
CREATE ROLE fantacalcio_app LOGIN PASSWORD '<generated-secret>';
CREATE DATABASE fantacalcio_intelligence OWNER fantacalcio_app ENCODING 'UTF8';
```

Restrict network access to the application host, require TLS when the database is remote, and keep administrative credentials separate. The application role must own or be permitted to migrate its application schema because Flyway runs during startup.

## 3. Database credentials

Place the JDBC URL, username and password in the deployment secret store. Use the real variables from `backend/.env.production.example`:

```text
DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://<db-host>:5432/fantacalcio_intelligence
DATABASE_USERNAME=<application-role>
DATABASE_PASSWORD=<secret>
```

Never pass secrets on a process command line, place them in frontend `VITE_*` variables, commit them, or include them in deployment logs.

## 4. Backend environment

Required:

```text
SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod
DATABASE_URL
DATABASE_USERNAME
DATABASE_PASSWORD
ADMIN_USERNAME
ADMIN_PASSWORD
APP_USER_USERNAME
APP_USER_PASSWORD
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://<app-domain>
```

Optional settings and certified defaults are documented in `backend/.env.production.example`. Keep source ingestion, listone sync, Transfermarkt discovery, identity automation and the data-refresh scheduler disabled for the first deployment. Enable each only after monitoring and source policies are approved.

For a same-origin reverse proxy, browser CORS is normally not exercised, but `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is still required by backend startup. Set it to the exact public HTTPS application origin, never `*` and never a trailing path.

## 5. Backend artifact

Build from a clean release checkout using only the wrapper:

```powershell
Set-Location "C:\path\to\fantacalcio-intelligence\backend"
.\mvnw.cmd clean test
.\mvnw.cmd clean package
```

On the managed Codex shell, if Maven resolves `user.home` incorrectly, invoke this same wrapper through `cmd.exe` and pass an explicit local repository. This is a build-machine accommodation, not a production runtime requirement. Do not substitute a globally installed Maven binary.

Publish `backend/target/backend-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar` to the new release directory. Record its SHA-256 checksum and retain the prior JAR for rollback.

## 6. Flyway migration

The JAR contains migrations from `classpath:db/migration`, currently through V69 (including V66.1). Startup uses `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`, Flyway validation, forward migration, `clean-disabled=true` and `baseline-on-migrate=false`.

Before first production startup:

1. take and verify a PostgreSQL backup;
2. restore that backup into an isolated rehearsal database when possible;
3. start the candidate JAR against rehearsal with `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod`;
4. confirm Flyway validates all migrations and reaches V69;
5. confirm legacy synthetic records are absent after V34/V59 cleanup;
6. stop rehearsal and only then approve production migration.

Never edit an already-applied migration or run `flyway clean`. Flyway Community does not provide automatic down migrations; database rollback is backup/restore.

## 7. Backend startup

Use a process supervisor (systemd or provider equivalent) and load secrets from `/etc/fantacalcio/backend.env`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Fantacalcio Intelligence backend
After=network-online.target

[Service]
User=fantacalcio
WorkingDirectory=/opt/fantacalcio/current
EnvironmentFile=/etc/fantacalcio/backend.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/java -jar /opt/fantacalcio/current/backend.jar
SuccessExitStatus=143
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
TimeoutStopSec=30
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Keep backend port 8080 private to the host/network. Allow graceful shutdown to complete before forcing termination.

## 8. Backend health

Infrastructure probes already exist:

```text
GET /actuator/health/liveness
GET /actuator/health/readiness
```

Production hides health details. Readiness includes application/database health through Spring Boot Actuator. Also verify the public application endpoint `GET /api/v1/system/status`, which executes a database query and should return HTTP 200 with `status: UP`.

Do not route traffic until readiness is `UP`. An unauthenticated admin request must be rejected, while valid admin credentials must succeed over HTTPS.

## 9. Frontend environment and build

Use `frontend/.env.production.example` as the source of public build-time values:

```text
VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/v1
VITE_FATAL_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT=
```

`VITE_DEV_PROXY_TARGET` is development-only and must not be set for production. Build with Node 22/npm 10+:

```powershell
Set-Location "C:\path\to\fantacalcio-intelligence\frontend"
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run test:run
npm run build
npm run format:check
```

Verify `dist/index.html`, hashed JS/CSS assets, lazy chunks, no `.map`, no MSW worker, no localhost telemetry endpoint and no secret. Publish only `dist/`.

## 10. Frontend publishing

Copy `dist/` into `/opt/fantacalcio/releases/<release-id>/frontend/`. Do not overwrite the active release in place. Switch the `current` symlink only after backend readiness and proxy configuration validation.

Cache hashed `/assets/*` as immutable for one year. Serve `index.html` with `no-cache` or `must-revalidate` so releases can switch safely.

## 11. Reverse proxy

The required topology is same-origin:

```text
Internet -> HTTPS reverse proxy
                    +-> /api/v1/*  -> 127.0.0.1:8080
                    +-> /actuator/* -> 127.0.0.1:8080 (restrict externally if provider probes internally)
                    +-> /*          -> frontend dist
```

Provider-neutral Nginx-shaped example (validate syntax on the selected host):

```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name APP_DOMAIN;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name APP_DOMAIN;
    root /opt/fantacalcio/current/frontend;

    location /api/v1/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
        proxy_set_header Content-Type $content_type;
        proxy_read_timeout 60s;
    }

    location /actuator/health/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location /assets/ {
        try_files $uri =404;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" always;
    }

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache" always;
    }
}
```

The `proxy_pass` form intentionally preserves `/api/v1/`. Verify this behavior on the selected reverse proxy before release.

## 12. HTTPS

- Terminate TLS at the reverse proxy with a trusted certificate.
- Redirect all HTTP to HTTPS before enabling Basic Auth traffic.
- Enable automatic certificate renewal and monitor expiry.
- After HTTPS is verified, set `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`. Add `preload` only after every subdomain is permanently HTTPS-ready.
- Never expose port 8080 publicly.

## 13. CORS

Set `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to the exact public application origin, for example `https://app.example.com`. Multiple approved origins are comma-separated. Wildcard origins are rejected by startup. The backend allows the required methods and `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`, and `Cache-Control` request headers with credentials enabled.

Same-origin `/api/v1` is preferred and avoids cross-origin browser traffic. CORS remains defense-in-depth for direct backend access and alternate approved origins.

## 14. Security headers

Apply at the reverse proxy after testing the candidate release:

```text
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' <telemetry-origin-if-enabled>; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()
```

Do not add `'unsafe-inline'` or a telemetry origin unless runtime verification proves it necessary. If telemetry is enabled, add only its HTTPS origin to `connect-src`. `frame-ancestors 'none'` is the primary framing control; `X-Frame-Options: DENY` may be added for legacy clients.

## 15. Telemetry

Telemetry is optional for the first deployment. If no endpoint is configured, the frontend selects `NoopFatalTelemetryProvider` and deployment remains valid.

To activate real telemetry, set `VITE_FATAL_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` before `npm run build`. The endpoint must be HTTPS, accept CORS POST requests, and be privacy-approved. It receives only `eventType`, `source`, `errorName`, `timestamp`, and route pathname; never error message, stack, Basic credentials or business data. Add the telemetry origin to CSP `connect-src`.

## 16. Smoke test

After switching the candidate release:

1. verify HTTP redirects to HTTPS;
2. verify liveness, readiness and `/api/v1/system/status` return HTTP 200/`UP`;
3. test `/`, `/players`, a real player detail, `/auction`, `/lineup`, `/calendar`, `/scouting` and a frontend 404;
4. test login, `/squad`, `/admin`, `/profile`, logout and refresh losing in-memory auth;
5. verify direct navigation to every SPA route returns the app, not proxy 404;
6. verify dark/light and 390/768/1440 layouts;
7. verify browser console has zero errors, React warnings and uncaught exceptions;
8. verify unauthenticated admin/API mutation access is rejected;
9. if telemetry is enabled, use a controlled synthetic fatal test only in an approved non-production/rehearsal environment and inspect the privacy-safe payload.

## 17. Backup

Take a logical backup immediately before every migration-bearing deployment. PostgreSQL 17 example:

```bash
PGPASSWORD="$DATABASE_PASSWORD" pg_dump \
  --host="$DB_HOST" --port=5432 --username="$DATABASE_USERNAME" \
  --format=custom --compress=9 --file="fantacalcio-predeploy-${RELEASE_ID}.dump" \
  fantacalcio_intelligence
```

Store backups encrypted outside the VM, record checksum/size/tool version, and test restore regularly. Prefer provider snapshots/PITR in addition to `pg_dump`, not instead of it.

## 18. Restore

Restore into a new empty database first; do not overwrite production until the rollback decision is approved:

```bash
createdb --host="$DB_HOST" --username="$DB_ADMIN_USER" fantacalcio_restore
PGPASSWORD="$DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" pg_restore \
  --host="$DB_HOST" --username="$DB_ADMIN_USER" \
  --dbname=fantacalcio_restore --clean --if-exists --no-owner \
  "fantacalcio-predeploy-${RELEASE_ID}.dump"
```

Validate Flyway history, row counts, health and representative reads. For an actual rollback, stop application writes, restore/swap the database under a documented maintenance window, then start the compatible prior JAR.

## 19. Rollback

Frontend rollback:

1. repoint `current/frontend` to the prior immutable release;
2. reload the reverse proxy;
3. purge only `index.html`/HTML cache, not hashed assets;
4. repeat public/direct-route smoke tests.

Backend rollback without schema incompatibility:

1. stop the candidate gracefully;
2. repoint `current/backend.jar` to the prior JAR;
3. restore the prior environment/config version;
4. start and verify readiness/system status.

Database rollback:

- Never assume Flyway can downgrade automatically.
- If the new migration is backward-compatible, the prior JAR may run against the migrated schema after explicit verification.
- If incompatible or data was transformed, stop writes and restore the pre-deploy backup/PITR into a new database, switch `DATABASE_URL`, then start the prior JAR.
- Preserve the failed database and logs for investigation.

Configuration rollback:

Keep versioned, secret-free config templates with each release and versioned secret-manager revisions. Restore the prior values atomically; never copy secrets into Git or command history.

## D02 approval inputs

D02 must not start until the owner supplies or approves: cloud/provider and region, VM sizing, managed PostgreSQL plan, domain/DNS control, TLS method, production database identifiers/credentials through a secret channel, admin/user usernames and passwords through a secret channel, backup retention/RPO/RTO, monitoring/log retention, and the optional telemetry decision/endpoint.

--- FILE: backend\src\main\java\it\fantacalciointelligence\backend\auction\AuctionApiPriceService.java ---
package it.fantacalciointelligence.backend.auction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.RoundingMode;
import java.util.List;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import it.fantacalciointelligence.backend.common.ResourceNotFoundException;

@Service
public class AuctionApiPriceService {

    private final B67AuctionPriceModelService modelService;

    public AuctionApiPriceService(
            B67AuctionPriceModelService modelService
    ) {
        this.modelService = modelService;
    }

    /**
     * Public Auction API adapter.
     *
     * B67 is the current read model.
     * B51 remains immutable historical evidence.
     *
     * Public GET endpoints remain read-only and have no
     * persistence side effects.
     */
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public AuctionPriceResponse calculate(
            Long playerId,
            String seasonCode,
            int budget,
            int teams,
            boolean defenseModifier
    ) {

        B67AuctionPriceModelService.AuctionPriceModelResult result =
                modelService.calculateAll(
                                seasonCode,
                                budget,
                                teams,
                                defenseModifier
                        )
                        .stream()
                        .filter(item ->
                                item.playerId().equals(
                                        playerId
                                )
                        )
                        .findFirst()
                        .orElseThrow(() ->
                                new ResourceNotFoundException(
                                        "Giocatore non trovato"
                                )
                        );

        if (!"PRICED".equals(result.pricingStatus())) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Prezzo asta non disponibile: evidenza insufficiente"
            );
        }

        return toResponse(
                result,
                teams,
                budget,
                defenseModifier
        );
    }

    /**
     * Calculates the complete current B67 auction market once.
     * Used by ranking and downstream intelligence.
     */
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public List<AuctionPriceResponse> calculateAll(
            String seasonCode,
            int budget,
            int teams,
            boolean defenseModifier
    ) {

        return modelService.calculateAll(
                        seasonCode,
                        budget,
                        teams,
                        defenseModifier
                )
                .stream()
                .filter(result ->
                        "PRICED".equals(
                                result.pricingStatus()
                        )
                )
                .map(result ->
                        toResponse(
                                result,
                                teams,
                                budget,
                                defenseModifier
                        )
                )
                .toList();
    }

    private AuctionPriceResponse toResponse(
            B67AuctionPriceModelService.AuctionPriceModelResult result,
            int teams,
            int budget,
            boolean defenseModifier
    ) {

        BigDecimal calculationScore =
                BigDecimal
                        .valueOf(
                                result.auctionScore()
                        )
                        .setScale(
                                2,
                                RoundingMode.HALF_UP
                        );

        String explanation =
                String.format(
                        "Prezzo calcolato con %s. "
                                + "Score asta %.2f/100, "
                                + "rank ruolo %d, "
                                + "percentile ruolo %.2f/100, "
                                + "evidenza %s.",
                        B67AuctionPriceModelService.ALGORITHM_VERSION,
                        result.auctionScore(),
                        result.auctionRoleRank(),
                        result.auctionRolePercentile(),
                        result.evidenceTier()
                );

        return new AuctionPriceResponse(
                result.playerId(),
                result.playerName(),
                result.club(),
                result.role(),
                teams,
                budget,
                defenseModifier,
                result.minimumPrice(),
                result.recommendedPrice(),
                result.maximumPrice(),
                result.budgetPercentage(),
                calculationScore,
                result.pricingStatus(),
                explanation
        );
    }
}
